spec.title: codkit PROP-001: Purpose, boundaries, MVP scope

status.comment: a self-contained contract for standalone Codkit; the detail is sufficient for implementation without external product context

p.IMPLEMENTER-CONTRACT: The specifications of the codkit module are written for a worker who took no part in the design and has no access to the reference repositories (clean room, `common/PROP-004`). Every design decision is already made; the implementer makes no design decisions and reads no references; when a fact about upstream is missing, the implementer reads the fork tree at the pin (this is allowed) or stops and asks the owner.

p.module-doc-map: Module contents: PROP-001 purpose (this document); PROP-002 layout and launch; PROP-003 configuration and data conventions; PROP-004 markers and patch format; PROP-005 delta layers; PROP-006 application metadata, locking, inventory; PROP-007 CLI commands; PROP-008 engines (load/save/classification/renames/reason); PROP-009 the cycle orchestrator; PROP-010 integration with the build of the fork tree - code delivery, the watch daemons, the tests; PROP-011 CI and the air-gapped circuit; PROP-012 output, errors, NFRs, documentation, open decision points; PROP-013 testing of codkit itself; PROP-014 the standards package and licence annotation; PROP-015 the delivery of the Codkit runtime - `runtime load|check`, `gen`, the delivered files (the content of the library belongs to the project type); FEAT-001 the polygon; FEAT-002 acceptance scenarios; FEAT-003/004 the requirement specifications for the human and the agent protocol. PROP-016 project types - the contract between the engine and a project type (`vscode`, `generic`, `theia`), types as packages, the split of the specifications into `modules/codkit` and `modules/vscode`. The answers of the `vscode` type live in the module `modules/vscode` (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-001#VSCODE-MODULE-MAP`).

facts.DOES-RESOLVE-TREE: Resolves the path to the fork tree and checks its fitness (PROP-008 §1–2).
facts.DOES-SYNC: Tombstone (Phase 1 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, 2026-09-06): the anchor is replaced by `DOES-LOAD` below; this anchor's address is immutable (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR). The name reservation has been honoured: since Phase 8 of that campaign (2026-09-06) `codkit sync` is a real two-way save+load command, the live contract is PROP-007 `##CMD-SYNC-TWO-WAY` and the algorithm is PROP-008 §5a.
facts.DOES-LOAD: Brings the fork tree to the pin and applies the delta as commits on a disposable generated branch (`load`), and delivers own code by copying.
facts.DOES-EXTRACT: Extracts edits from the tree into patch-set artifacts (`save`/extract) and protects against the silent loss of work (the drift guard).
facts.DOES-LAYERS: Maintains the delta layers (PROP-005), the markers (PROP-004), the inventory (PROP-006).
facts.DOES-BUILD-WRAP: Wraps the build watch daemons of the project type into the commands `build up|down|status|errors` (PROP-010).
facts.DOES-CYCLE: Orchestrates the pin upgrade cycle with outcome classification, reasons, a journal and resumability (`cycle`, PROP-009), and gives a daily forecast (`forecast`).
facts.DOES-PUBLISH: Publishes the generated branches to the hosted fork repository (`publish`, `common/PROP-002` §4).
facts.DOES-CI: Gives a containerized CI run «from scratch» with no network (`ci`, PROP-011) and race guards (`common/PROP-002` §7).

facts.NOT-CONSUMER-PRODUCT: Does not define or develop the user-facing product that a particular patch set serves; such requirements belong to the external consumer.
facts.NOT-HISTORY: Does not rewrite patch-set history; does not commit into the fork tree «by hand» (the generated commits of the delta branch are not manual).
facts.NOT-NET-IN-CI: Does not touch the network in `--ci` mode at all; locally only explicit commands do (`clone`, `--clone-if-missing`, `publish`).
facts.NOT-REJECTED-MODELS: Does not rebase the delta, squash cycles, infer state from heuristics, or make the main path interactive (the non-goals of `common/PROP-001` §4).
facts.NOT-UPSTREAM-AI-FILES: Does not edit upstream files with AI instructions in the tree (`AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and the like) and does not execute them.

td.LATER-RULE-ENGINE: the rewrite-rule engine (its format and validation are in the MVP)

td.MVP-SYNC-SAVE: Tombstone (Phase 1 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, 2026-09-06): the anchor is replaced by `MVP-LOAD-SAVE` (see below, outside the table); the address is immutable (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR). The pair `load`+`save` was joined by the two-way `sync` in Phase 8 of that campaign - PROP-007 `##CMD-SYNC-TWO-WAY`.

td.LATER-NLS: a strings/nls layer beyond the prefix rule

td.MVP-LAYERS: the own / service-override / entry-module / config-overlay / resource-file / patch layers

td.MVP-MARKERS: markers plus the parser/validator; the hide sample; the removed registry; contract/guard tests

td.LATER-UPSTREAM-TEST-FILTERS: the full circuit of upstream test filters

td.MVP-INVENTORY: the inventory plus its checks plus `verify`

td.LATER-OWNER-ROUTING: automatic routing of notifications to owners

td.LATER-DASHBOARD: a metrics dashboard (the series are collected from the MVP on)

td.LATER-FULL-CYCLE: the extended `cycle` (full automation of the phases)

p.MVP-LOAD-SAVE: `load`/`save` with idempotence and fingerprint metadata - the successor of the tombstone `MVP-SYNC-SAVE` in the table above (Phase 1 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE).

p.MVP-BUILD-ORDER: The build order is «foundation first, superstructure second»: independent resolution of the three roots → apply/extract → inventory/layers → orchestrator → rules/agents. The execution plan may change and is not part of the permanent specification.

p.MVP-ACCEPTANCE: The MVP is accepted when: scenarios S01–S14 of FEAT-002 are green; the FEAT-001 polygon contains every layer; the NFRs of PROP-012 §3 are measured; the documentation of PROP-012 §4 exists; the clean-room check of `common/PROP-004` passes.
